nodes.label: Cluster singleton
nodes.rationale: Exactly one instance cluster-wide, on the leader, respawned by the next elected leader. Trades some unavailability at failover for the strong 'exactly one instance' invariant, so it is not a low-latency failover tool. If you would write if (!alreadyExists) spawn(...), this is probably the right thing.

nodes.label: ClusterSingletonProxy
nodes.rationale: What start and ref both return: an ordinary forwarding ActorRef, so a singleton is passed around like any other actor and no consumer signature needs to know. ref.stop() is a warning no-op because elsewhere stop() sends a PoisonPill, which here would kill whatever the current leader hosts.

nodes.label: SingletonKey
nodes.rationale: Declared as static readonly singleton so name and message type are not repeated at the call site. The explicit type argument is load-bearing — without it the key infers SingletonKey<unknown> and every derived ref degrades.

nodes.label: start vs ref
nodes.rationale: start puts the node into the rotation, ref only addresses — the counterpart to ClusterSharding.startProxy. Both return the same memoised ref for a key and the local manager is resolved per delivery, so a node that later calls start keeps the ref and simply delivers locally. Call start on every node that can become leader, or nothing hosts and messages dead-letter.

nodes.label: bufferSize
nodes.rationale: Caps what the proxy holds while no node hosts — normally one gossip round, unbounded in an outage. Beyond the 1000 default messages dead-letter with a warning. The buffer flushes on the first event that could have produced a host, not only a leader change: for a role-restricted singleton the first role-carrying member can join without the leader changing at all, and before v0.17.0 that left the buffer unflushed indefinitely while every later send routed normally.

nodes.label: Role belongs on the key
nodes.rationale: A role is not part of identity (two keys are equal iff their names match) — it rides along so every node reads the same one. A node that only calls ref has no options object, so a role set solely via withRole is invisible to it and its proxy would resolve a different host than the managers.

nodes.label: No SingletonActor interface
nodes.rationale: TypeScript's implements checks only the instance side — there is no static implements and abstract static is a compile error — so a marker interface would be structurally empty. A static field works, composes with any base class (a singleton is often also a PersistentActor, and TS has single inheritance), and enforcement happens at the start call site, which derives the message type from both key and actor position and reports a mismatch.

nodes.label: Singleton failover
nodes.rationale: Detection via gossip, deterministic re-election by member sort order, spawn on the new leader, then proxies shift their forwarding target. The window is bounded by the failure detector's timeout; in-flight messages dead-letter unless durability is configured. Stopping is asynchronous: the manager releases lease and envelope path in postStop and the actor name stays taken until termination completes, so restarting the same singleton in the same turn throws with an explanation.
